A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TAVT research and provide readable methods, equations, results, figures and appendices. Content can be matched despite renumbering, added subsections and relocation of the limitations discussion.

before.justification: v1 reports original MuJoCo and MetaWorld experiments, including benchmark comparisons, representation visualizations, component ablations and exploration analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds a two-dimensional latent experiment, a finer regularization sweep and computational timing measurements.

M1.justification: The bisimulation and on-off losses, task-preserving WGAN, virtual-task construction, exploration policy and state regularization remain unchanged, including Algorithms 1–2 and Appendix D. The new two-dimensional latent experiment tests a configuration of the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six MuJoCo and six MetaWorld ML1 settings, including the retained interpolation and extrapolation scenarios. New supplementary experiments use existing environments. ML10 and ML45 are mentioned only as limitations, not evaluated.

E2.justification: The matched benchmark comparisons retain MAML, RL2, VariBad, LDM, PEARL, CCM, Amago and MIER. Representation comparisons and existing component comparisons also retain their participants. The new timing study reuses PEARL and existing TAVT variants.

E3.justification: Appendix B.2 adds an Ant-Goal-OOD experiment using two latent dimensions instead of the default ten. Appendix C.2 adds regularization coefficients 0.05 and 0.2 to the existing sweep, and Appendix H.2 introduces relative per-epoch timing. Existing benchmark splits, budgets and default configurations remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a direct latent-geometry check without t-SNE, a finer Walker-Mass-OOD regularization and estimation-bias analysis, and a component timing breakdown. These are focused extensions to the retained component, context-error, exploration and mixing-coefficient analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions state that performance comparisons average five random seeds and report standard deviations through shading or ± values. No revised run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table H.1 newly reports relative epoch times of 100%, 103%, 111%, 116% and 118% for PEARL, Recon only, TAVT without Lgen, TAVT without on-off loss and full TAVT. Figures B.3 and C.3 add latent and regularization results; 0.1 remains the best-return coefficient. Existing benchmark scores and curves are retained.

T1.justification: The bisimulation definition, metric proposition, Appendix A proof and mathematical derivations are unchanged. Appendix A corrects definition and proposition numbering to match the main text; this does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: metric-based task representations, task-preserving virtual samples and state regularization improve OOD generalization. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly qualifies t-SNE's distance interpretation and adds the limitation that TAVT covers parametric task distributions, excluding semantically distinct ML10/ML45 tasks. Compared with v1 Appendix J, Section 6 softens the hyperparameter warning and omits the explicit memory/I/O limitation; Appendix H.2 interprets measured training overhead as practical.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a TAVT repository link in the abstract and Appendix G.3, clarifies dense MuJoCo rewards and the Ant-Goal-OOD episode horizon, and reports relative training time. Hardware, network sizes, loss coefficients and detailed implementation algorithms remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the already-evaluated RL2 and Amago baselines, citing Duan et al. (2016) and Grigsby et al. (2024), and removes Chae et al. (2022) and Yeom et al. (2024). The broader research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 corrects template headers, wording and several cross-references, moves and revises limitations into Section 6, introduces subsections within Appendices B, C and H, and adds acknowledgments. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds Figures B.3 and C.3 and Table H.1. Its new main-text Figure 6 recombines environment illustrations already present in the appendices. Existing figures receive sizing, panel-label and caption refinements, with corresponding relocation and renumbering.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful checks of latent geometry and regularization, quantifies computational overhead, supplies a TAVT code link and clarifies the parametric-task applicability boundary. These improve support and transparency while retaining the main evidence. The gain is limited: the new analyses are narrow, timing is only relative, and v1's explicit memory-use limitation is omitted.
